title: Palace wants closer look at 'China money' linked to VP husband's firm

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Friday said former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV’s claim that a firm linked to Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband received more than P319 million from China should be not be taken lightly, if backed by sufficient evidence. At a press conference, Trillanes said CALE88 Foods Corp., a food company partly owned by Atty. Mans Carpio, received hundreds of millions of pesos from China, which he said raised serious national security concerns.
